title: Checkpoint: World Power, Boom and Bust
objective: After this level you can explain how war, boom and depression between 1898 and 1945 made the US a world power with a bigger federal government.
summary: From an overseas empire in 1898 to victory in 1945, war, boom and depression made the US a world power with a much bigger federal government.

cards.headline: Chapter 8 finale: about 334,000 in uniform in 1939, over 12 million by 1945.
cards.body: Between 1898 and 1945, wars, a boom and a depression made the US a world power with a far bigger federal government. Let's put the chapter on one timeline.

cards.headline: From the Treaty of Paris to Tokyo Bay

events.label: Spain cedes Puerto Rico and Guam and sells the Philippines
The US declares war on Germany
The stock market crashes on Black Tuesday
The Social Security Act is signed

cards.headline: A bigger government, a bigger role
cards.body: Before the Great Depression, federal spending was less than 3 percent of GDP; by 1939 it topped 10 percent, as the New Deal built programs like Social Security. War did the rest, from colonies won in 1898 to a military of over 12 million. Not everyone shared the gains: Mexican Americans were pushed out and Japanese Americans were incarcerated. Yet the war also reopened one door: in 1943 Congress repealed Chinese exclusion, while China was an ally.

cards.headline: Chapter 8 complete
learned: How war and depression made the US a world power with a much bigger federal government.
Why Americans argued over empire in 1898, joining World War I and the atomic bomb.
What the Great Migration, Prohibition and the Dust Bowl changed in everyday life.
Who was left out or pushed out, from Social Security to Japanese American incarceration.

questions.prompt: World Power, Boom and Bust: which order of events is right?

options.label: Black Tuesday, the Treaty of Paris, Pearl Harbor
options.rationale: The Treaty of Paris (1898) came before the crash (1929).

options.label: The Treaty of Paris, Pearl Harbor, Black Tuesday
options.rationale: Black Tuesday (1929) came before Pearl Harbor (1941).

options.label: The Treaty of Paris, Black Tuesday, Pearl Harbor
Pearl Harbor, the Treaty of Paris, Black Tuesday

questions.explanation: The Treaty of Paris was signed in 1898, the market crashed in 1929 and Japan attacked Pearl Harbor in 1941.

questions.prompt: How much did the US military grow between 1939 and 1945?

options.label: From about 334,000 people to over 12 million
From about 12 million to 334,000
From about 3 million to 4 million
It stayed about the same

questions.explanation: The US military grew from about 334,000 people in 1939 to over 12 million in 1945.

questions.prompt: How did the Depression years change the size of the federal government?

options.label: Federal spending fell below 3 percent of GDP
Federal spending rose from under 3 percent of GDP to over 10 percent by 1939
The federal government handed its programs to the states
options.rationale: The New Deal built federal programs.

options.label: Nothing changed until 1945

questions.explanation: Federal spending rose from less than 3 percent of GDP before the Depression to over 10 percent by 1939.

questions.prompt: Which group was forced into camps under Executive Order 9066?

options.label: German Americans
options.rationale: The order led to the removal of Japanese Americans.

options.label: Mexican Americans
options.rationale: They were pushed to Mexico in the 1930s, not held in camps.

options.label: Chinese Americans
Japanese Americans

questions.explanation: Executive Order 9066 led to the forced removal of about 122,000 Japanese Americans from the West Coast.

questions.prompt: Level 66's Chinese Exclusion Act of 1882 shut out Chinese laborers. What happened to the exclusion laws during World War II?

options.label: They were extended to all of Asia
Congress repealed them in 1943, while China was an ally
The Supreme Court upheld them in 1944
options.rationale: That was the Korematsu ruling, about Japanese Americans.

options.label: Nothing: they lasted until 1965

questions.explanation: Congress repealed the Chinese exclusion laws in 1943, when China was a World War II ally.
